correctness.rationale: The affine contraction gives the unique stationary series. Its support is the compact fixed point of the contracting support operator; adding [0,1/3] fills the gaps of the scaled Cantor set (maximal gap 2/9). Grouping the centred independent signs by n+k=m gives m copies with coefficient 2/3^(m+1). Choose m so the m-th angle is u in [π/3,π]; its product with the next cosine has absolute value at most 9/16 by the quadratic 4z²−3z, z=cos²(u/3), or the bound 1/2 on the lower half of the range. This gives Fourier decay with exponent log_3(16/9)>1/2 and Plancherel yields the stated strict lower Sobolev range. At the stated t_N all angles through m=N are integer multiples of π; the remaining factors are positive and give BA^N. The tail-deficit bound A≥(1−π²/144)/2>4/9 implies unbounded t_N|μ̂(t_N)|, incompatible with a finite derivative measure of the BV zero extension (finite one-sided traces). Fixed-width bands around t_N retain a uniform positive fraction of A^N: the early product has summable cosine deficits and the late log ratio is bounded by O((N+1)3^(−N)) away from zeros. Summing the band contributions diverges also at the stated endpoint. Independent finite products reproduced A, B, s_* and the sampled resonances; the analytic estimates, not samples, cover all N and stated Sobolev exponents.
residual_risks: Neither optimal Sobolev threshold nor continuity is determined; no implication for other contractions or Cantor weights.

value.rationale: The matching-scale Cantor example separates an interval attractor and genuine L² regularization from BV regularization in a natural singular-noise affine model. The lacunary mechanism and fixed-band Sobolev obstruction give quantitative information beyond testing a sufficient smoothing criterion or finding one large Fourier value.
residual_risks: The value is a concrete regularity boundary/counterexample, not optimal regularity or a parameter classification.
